newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to hire more guards to protect embassies.
newsitem.headline: Japan to hire more guards to protect embassies.

text.p: Japan is to hire more security guards to protect its diplomatic offices overseas from terrorist attack following the hostage crisis in Peru, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said on Tuesday.
He said the number of locally hired guards would be increased by 370 next year so that diplomatic buildings could be guarded around the clock.

The number of Japanese security experts sent to protect overseas diplomatic buildings would also be raised by 16 to 171. The cost of hiring more security staff would amount to around 620 million yen ($5.43 million) in the year starting next April, Ikeda said.
Other emergency measures would include setting up bomb detectors in and around diplomatic buildings as well as strengthening and elevating fences around embassies, he said.
But it was still unclear how much money would be allocated for those measures, he added.
He declined to say which diplomatic establishments abroad were thought to need more security.
Japan will spend about 2.5 billion yen ($21.9 million) on security at overseas diplomatic buildings in the year starting in April, a ministry official said.

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru, on December 17 during a reception to mark Emperor Akihito's birthday, taking more than 500 hostages.
Despite freeing a large number of captives, the rebels still hold dozens of top Peruvian government officials and about 30 high-ranking Japanese businessmen and diplomats. ($1=114 yen)
